title: ULID mandate inconsistency across non-time-ordered IDs
description:
File: draft-atwood-jmap-chat-00.md
Locations: lines 562, 610, 642, 688, 741, 766, 784

Seven id-field definitions mandate ULID:
- SpaceRole.id (line 562)
- Category.id (line 610)
- Space.id (line 642)
- CustomEmoji.id (line 688)
- SpaceBan.id (line 741)
- ReadPosition.id (line 766)
- PresenceStatus.id (line 784)

Each says (with minor wording variation): "A ULID assigned by the server."

ULID is genuinely required for Chat.id, Message.id, and senderMsgId because the spec relies on lexicographic-time ordering of those values (Chat.unreadCount at line 439, message ordering at line 467). The seven types above are opaque server-assigned identifiers with no documented protocol reliance on the ULID property.

Internal-inconsistency evidence: SpaceInvite.id at line 710 already uses generic "Opaque server-assigned JMAP identifier" wording. The corpus is inconsistent with itself.

A deployment using KSUID, Snowflake, or RFC 8620-style opaque random strings for these seven types produces no client-observable difference.
acceptance_criteria:
- The seven id-field definitions use "Opaque server-assigned JMAP identifier" wording (matching SpaceInvite.id line 710)
- Chat.id, Message.id, and senderMsgId retain explicit ULID requirement (time-ordering dependency)
- grep '\\bULID\\b' returns only the legitimate time-ordered cases plus any historical context references
- No behavior change in the federation or push drafts (they reference `senderMsgId` only)
